title: 8-Register File: 2 Read Ports, 1 Write Port
statement: Design an 8-register file with two asynchronous read ports and one synchronous write port. Reads should return the contents of addressed registers immediately, while writes occur on the clock edge. A synchronous reset should clear all registers to zero.
module_signature: module register_file_8x8_2r1w(input clk, input rst, input write_en, input [2:0] write_addr, input [7:0] write_data, input [2:0] read_addr_a, input [2:0] read_addr_b, output [7:0] read_data_a, output [7:0] read_data_b);
behavior: read_data_a and read_data_b reflect the contents at the read addresses.
write occurs on the rising edge when write_en is 1.
rst synchronously clears all registers to zero.
All state updates occur on the rising edge of clk.
rst is active-high and synchronous unless the problem statement explicitly says otherwise.
Use non-blocking assignments in clocked always blocks.
Outputs must never depend on uninitialized x/z state after reset.
When rst is asserted on a rising edge, registered outputs reset to their documented initial values.
constraints: Do not use asynchronous writes or multi-clock memories.
hint: Implement the register file as an array of flip-flops indexed by address.
